arxiv-2108-06355.title: Boundary dynamics in competing critical black hole formation
arxiv-2108-06355.creator: Cole Kelson-Packer, John Belz
arxiv-2108-06355.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Cole Kelson-Packer, John Belz. Expanding upon our previous study of competing critical phenomena in black hole formation, we numerically investigate the behavior of dominant exponents across the boundary separating asymptotically dispersing and collapsing regions in a two-dimensional configuration space of initial data. We find that across the Type II boundary section the dominant exponent remains constant, equal to the reciprocal of Choptuik’s well-known quasi-universal value, whereas across the Type I section the exponent noticeably varies.

arxiv-2208-03001.title: Born-Oppenheimer and the Geometry of Ray Space: an application to cold atoms
arxiv-2208-03001.creator: Joseph Samuel
arxiv-2208-03001.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Joseph Samuel. It is known that, within the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, the slow modes of the nuclear motion are altered by three effects that emerge from integrating out the fast modes of the electronic motion. The first is an effective scalar potential V d ​ y ​ n V_{\mathrm{d}yn} coming from the eigenvalue of the electronic state, the second is an effective magnetic field coming from the Berry phase vector potential A A .

arxiv-2210-09769.title: STay-ON-the-Ridge: Guaranteed Convergence to Local Minimax Equilibrium in Nonconvex-Nonconcave Games
arxiv-2210-09769.description: Abstract Min-max optimization problems involving nonconvex-nonconcave objectives have found important applications in adversarial training and other multi-agent learning settings. Yet, no known gradient descent-based method is guaranteed to converge to (even local notions of) min-max equilibrium in the nonconvex-nonconcave setting.

arxiv-2302-06838.title: A novel approach for bilevel programs based on Wolfe duality Thanks: This work was supported in part by NSFC (Nos. 12071280, 11901380, 11971220).
arxiv-2302-06838.creator: Yuwei Li, Gui-Hua Lin, Jin Zhang, Xide Zhu
arxiv-2302-06838.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yuwei Li, Gui-Hua Lin, Jin Zhang, Xide Zhu. This paper considers a bilevel program, which has many applications in practice. To develop effective numerical algorithms, it is generally necessary to transform the bilevel program into a single-level optimization problem. The most popular approach is to replace the lower-level program by its KKT conditions and then the bilevel program can be reformulated as a mathematical program with equilibrium constraints (MPEC for short).

arxiv-2505-16225.title: MAPLE: Many-Shot Adaptive Pseudo-Labeling for In-Context Learning
arxiv-2505-16225.creator: Zihan Chen, Song Wang, Zhen Tan, Jundong Li, Cong Shen
arxiv-2505-16225.description: Abstract In-Context Learning (ICL) empowers Large Language Models (LLMs) to tackle diverse tasks by incorporating multiple input-output examples, known as demonstrations, into the input of LLMs. More recently, advancements in the expanded context windows of LLMs have led to many-shot ICL, which uses hundreds of demonstrations and outperforms few-shot ICL, which relies on fewer examples.

pmc-12285434.title: 복부 산통을 주소로 내원한 간내 폐흡충증 증례
pmc-12285434.creator: Min Sung Kim
pmc-12285434.description: In Korea, the prevalence of paragonimiasis has decreased markedly since 1970 and is now rarely encountered. Although the lung is the primary site of paragonimiasis, ectopic infestation can occur in other sites. The central nervous system is the most commonly involved ectopic site, accounting for only approximately 1% of all paragonimiasis patients.

pmc-12482301.title: Invasive pyogenic spondylitis with retropharyngeal and hepatic abscesses caused by hypermucoviscous klebsiella pneumoniae: A radiologic case report
pmc-12482301.creator: Ikki Nokita, Yukihito Nakamura, Shuntaro Matsuda
pmc-12482301.description: Hypermucoviscous Klebsiella pneumoniae (HmKP) is an emerging pathogen with strong invasive potential, particularly in immunocompromised patients. We present the case of an 84-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus who developed systemic infection including liver abscess, retropharyngeal abscess, and cervical pyogenic spondylitis caused by HmKP. Despite clinical improvement with appropriate antibiotics, follow-up MRI demonstrated vertebral collapse.

pmc-12602170.title: A Quantitative Spectrophotometric Assay Matched With Environmental Scanning Electron Microscopy to Measure Calcium Crystals in Human Osteoarthritic Synovial Fluid
pmc-12602170.creator: Michela Battistelli, Laura Valentini, Eleonora Olivotto
pmc-12602170.description: In the field of osteoarthritis (OA), the identification of reliable diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers in patients with hip lesions such as femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) could have an immeasurable value. Calcium crystal detection in synovial fluids (SFs) is one tool currently available to diagnose patients with rheumatologic disorders.

pmc-12604644.title: Stress, Stress Management, and Dementia: A Narrative Review
pmc-12604644.creator: Arunima Chaudhuri, Dharmendra K Gupta
pmc-12604644.description: Dementia represents a growing global health crisis, with age and genetics serving as primary risk factors alongside increasingly recognized modifiable contributors. Among these, chronic stress has gained attention as a significant factor that may accelerate cognitive decline and increase dementia risk. The biological mechanisms linking stress to dementia involve multiple pathways.

pmc-13582615.title: Comparative outcomes of neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy versus neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in locally advanced thoracic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a target trial emulation
pmc-13582615.creator: Zhiyu Li, Qiuxi Zhou, Qin Xie, Chenghao Wang, Lin Peng, Yongtao Han, Xuefeng Leng, Yan Miao, Qi Zhang, Wenwu He
pmc-13582615.description: BackgroundNeoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (NCRT) is standard for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), while neoadjuvant immune-chemotherapy (NICT) is a promising alternative. This study compared pathological response and long-term survival between NICT and NCRT followed by surgery using a target trial emulation framework.

pmc-13654330.title: Optical Coherence Tomography Findings Following Intravascular Lithotripsy in Calcified Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-13654330.creator: Giacomo Maria Cioffi, Stéphane Cook, Mario Togni, Julius Jonas Jelisejevas, Pascal Meier, Peter Wenaweser, Dorian Garin, Mehdi Madanchi, Natalia Pinilla-Echeverri, Karim M. Al-Azizi, Grigorios Tsigkas, Nicolas Amabile, Ioannis Skalidis
pmc-13654330.description: BackgroundIntravascular lithotripsy (IVL) has emerged as a novel technology for modifying calcified coronary lesions, whereas optical coherence tomography (OCT) enables high-resolution assessment of calcium modification and procedural outcomes. However, the mechanistic and procedural effects of IVL assessed by OCT across studies remain incompletely characterized.MethodsA systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261332946).
